record.original_question: Explain in what precise sense the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_mu(M), equipped with the right-invariant L2 metric, fails to be an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space, and relate that failure to the gap between sectional-curvature intuition and hydrodynamic stability.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. How “far” is Dµ (M ) from being an infinite-dimensional (locally) symmetric Rie- mannian space? This question is related to the following long standing (although little known) paradox. Con- sider the parallel sinusoidal steady fluid flow given by the stream function ψ = cos(k y) on the two-dimensional torus. Then well-known Arnold’s theorem claims that the sectional curvature of the group of exact area-preserving torus diffeomorphisms is nonpositive in all (and negative in most) two-dimensional directions containing the direction given by ψ, see [2, 6]. (There is a similar statement for a plane-parallel flow in a periodic channel.) Following Arnold’s idea on an intrinsic relation between negative curvature and the flow (Lagrangian) instability, one could expect that any plane-parallel flow is unstable. But this does not seem to be the case, since there are (Eulerian) stable parallel flows (for instance those with convex velocity profiles on “short tori”, see discussion in [6]), while Lagrangian and Eulerian instabilities are closely related, cf. [118]. The root of this misunderstanding lies in our “symmetric” intuition. In fact, this relation between the curvature sign and (in)stability of geodesics exists for symmetric spaces (say, on groups with bi-invariant metrics), see e.g. [97, 6]. On the other hand, the group Dµ (M ) is not symmetric, but rather “chiral”: as a Riemannian space it is somewhat twisted in one direction, and hence we observe a discrepancy between instability of geodesics and its negative curvature. The chirality of Dµ (M ) might have some other, more profound, consequences beyond the instability issues, which would be interesting to explore.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary) endowed with a smooth volume form $\mu$, and let $D_\mu(M)$ denote the group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$. Equip $D_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric obtained by right-translating the $L^2(\mu)$ inner product on divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$ (the Arnold metric, whose geodesics correspond to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations).

Recall that an infinite-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(N,g)$ is called locally symmetric if every point $p\in N$ admits a neighborhood on which the geodesic central reflection $\sigma_p$ (sending $\exp_p(v)\mapsto \exp_p(-v)$) is a local isometry; equivalently, the curvature tensor $R$ is parallel, $\nabla R\equiv 0$.

(a) Determine in what precise analytic and geometric sense $(D_\mu(M),\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{L^2})$ fails to be an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space. In particular, identify obstructions to $\nabla R = 0$ and to the geodesic reflections $\sigma_e$ at the identity being isometries of the right-invariant $L^2$ metric, and quantify "how far" $D_\mu(M)$ is from local symmetry (e.g.\ via $\nabla R$, via the failure of $\sigma_e$ to preserve the metric, or via the holonomy algebra).

(b) Use this failure of local symmetry to explain the apparent paradox arising for the parallel sinusoidal steady flow with stream function $\psi(x,y)=\cos(ky)$ on the flat two-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2$: Arnold's theorem asserts that the sectional curvature of $D_\mu(\mathbb{T}^2)$ is non-positive (and negative for most) two-planes containing the direction of $\psi$, which in a locally symmetric setting would suggest Lagrangian (and hence Eulerian) instability of the flow; yet such parallel flows can be Eulerian-stable (e.g.\ those with convex velocity profiles on sufficiently short tori). Reconcile this discrepancy by showing how the deviation of $D_\mu(M)$ from local symmetry breaks the symmetric-space heuristic linking negative sectional curvature to exponential divergence of geodesics, and thereby clarify the relationship between sign of curvature, Lagrangian instability, and Eulerian (hydrodynamic) stability.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how far the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group with its right-invariant L² metric is from being an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space, and its relation to the curvature/stability paradox for parallel flows, is listed as an open problem in recent surveys on geometric hydrodynamics. No published resolution was located; related work (e.g. on Misiołek curvature, semi-invariant metrics, totally geodesic subgroups) addresses adjacent questions but does not settle this one.

status_evidence.title: Arnold stability and Misiołek curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Studies relationships between Arnold/Eulerian stability and curvature criteria on diffeomorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate the curvature–stability link without resolving the symmetric-space question.
